title: Bootstrap the Discord bot application
body:
Create the discord.py client skeleton: token loaded from configuration, intents declared, and an entry point that starts the bot process.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Bot process starts and authenticates with a token from .env
- Missing/invalid token fails with a clear error message
- Lives entirely under the Discord adapter, per ADR-006 — no Core code references discord.py

title: Connect the bot to the Discord Gateway
body:
Handle the on_ready lifecycle event and log a successful Gateway connection, including which guilds the bot is in.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Bot logs a ready message with its username and guild count
- Reconnects gracefully on transient Gateway disconnects

title: Register slash command support
body:
Wire up discord.py's application command tree and sync it with Discord so slash commands are discoverable in the client.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Command tree syncs on startup (guild-scoped for fast iteration during development)
- Sync errors are logged instead of crashing the bot

title: Implement a /ping slash command
body:
A minimal health-check command to validate the slash command pipeline end-to-end.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- /ping replies with the bot's current Gateway latency
- Serves as the reference example for future slash commands

title: Define the Discord source adapter
body:
Per ADR-006, Discord is one input source adapter among several — it must translate discord.py's own callbacks into Core's source-agnostic domain events (SessionStarted, ParticipantJoined, ParticipantLeft) instead of Core reacting to discord.py types directly.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- A DiscordSourceAdapter implements the Core's input-source interface
- Joining/leaving a voice channel raises the corresponding Core events
- Core has zero direct dependency on discord.py types
